summary.title: What are some traits/practices of experienced/good programmers that every beginner programmer should know?
summary.one_liner: Learn the habits experienced programmers use, such as understanding the problem before coding, debugging by reasoning, keeping code simple, and testing pieces bottom-up.
keywords: stop assuming best case error handling
takeaways: Understand the business problem fully before writing code; wrong logic often produces no error, so it is hard to catch later.
Keep code simple and readable, avoid clever tricks and speculative generality, and only optimize after measuring.
Test and debug by reasoning, and break complex programs into small, testable functions, testing the lowest level first.
Learn your tools well (IDE, debugger, profiler, Git), and use search, error messages and code review as learning aids.
Communicate and collaborate: ask people for answers, pair program with more experienced developers, and take responsibility for mistakes.
summary.summary: This is a Quora thread with multiple answers to a question about habits of good programmers. The top answer lists 29 traits, such as using Google aggressively, skipping unnecessary meetings, and treating errors as clues. Other answers give more concrete advice: understand the requirement first, plan for failure cases, avoid over-engineering, and write neat code with comments and modular, top-down design. The page is opinion and anecdote rather than a structured tutorial, and it quotes a Brian Kernighan line about debugging. Some answers are long generic checklists that overlap heavily.
